clue.text: Nothing in the existing state provides sanctuary

parts.note: nothing is zero, the letter O
things left as they are are 'as is'

explanation.surface: An empty patch inside a country's borders serves as a place of refuge.
explanation.walkthrough: O goes inside AS IS.
explanation.definitionFit: A desert water-hole, or any calm retreat, is a refuge from hardship, a haven.

clue.text: Uninvolved, being in goal

explanation.surface: A detached outlook is the aim.
explanation.walkthrough: As an adjective it means impartial; as a noun, an aim.
explanation.definitionFit: Impartial and detached as an adjective; an aim or target as a noun.

clue.text: Answer no trumps, having enough in hand

parts.note: to answer a puzzle is to solve it
NT is the bridge abbreviation for no trumps

explanation.surface: A bridge player bids no trumps, holding enough strong cards.
explanation.definitionFit: Able to pay all debts, with money available.

clue.text: Fashions without line — such eye-sores

indicators.note: without tells us the letter for line is dropped

parts.note: styles are fashions

explanation.surface: Fashions lacking line are such ugly sights.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove L from STYLES. 'such' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Inflamed swellings on the eyelid, literally sore spots on the eye.

clue.text: Fat roll required for a blow-out

explanation.surface: A roll of fat is needed to cope with a big feast.
explanation.walkthrough: A blow-out is both a big meal (which builds a roll of fat) and a burst tyre (which needs a replacement carried in the boot).
explanation.definitionFit: Colloquially a waistline bulge is so called; literally it is the reserve wheel carried for a puncture.

clue.text: Drive by squadron leader to accept firm discipline

indicators.note: to accept means the joined pieces take the firm abbreviation inside them
by means one piece stands beside the other
the leader of a word is its first letter

parts.note: urge means drive, as an impulse
CO is the abbreviation for company, a firm

explanation.surface: A squadron leader's push to take on strict discipline.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drive' looks like a noun for a road trip; it is the push. S comes first, with CO tucked in after it.
explanation.definitionFit: To whip or punish harshly, chastise.

clue.text: Tailor attires public performer

indicators.note: to tailor something is to cut and reshape it, so these letters are refashioned

explanation.surface: A dressmaker clothes a stage entertainer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tailor' rearranges ATTIRES.
explanation.definitionFit: A professional entertainer such as a singer or dancer.

clue.text: One way a man may be taken from France

definitions.text: One way a man may be taken from France

parts.words: One way a man may be taken from France
parts.note: read as an abduction from France, but a 'man' is a chess piece and the capture is a pawn move, named with a French phrase meaning in passing

explanation.surface: A man might be kidnapped from France.
explanation.definitionFit: A chess capture of a pawn that has just advanced two squares, named in French ('in passing').

clue.text: Length of material needed to fabricate day gear

indicators.note: to fabricate is to construct, so these letters are built into a new word

explanation.surface: How much cloth is needed to make daytime clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to fabricate' rearranges DAY GEAR.
explanation.definitionFit: A measurement in yards, as of cloth.

clue.text: Standing to attention before the court

parts.note: ere is an old word for before

explanation.surface: Standing stiffly before a judge in court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Upright and straight, as a soldier on parade.

clue.text: Pleasure craft taking very old into club

parts.note: jolly is British slang for very, as in 'jolly good'

indicators.note: into tells us the abbreviation for old is put inside the word for club

parts.note: a bat is a club used in sport

explanation.surface: A leisure boat carries an aged person off to a nightclub.
explanation.walkthrough: JOLLY for 'very' is everyday British slang ('jolly good').
explanation.definitionFit: A small ship's boat used for rowing about, so a light craft for outings.

clue.text: Prize sum for contract

explanation.surface: A pot of prize money is offered for winning an agreement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'contract' is a verb here: to draw the lips together, as when one purses them.
explanation.definitionFit: Boxing prize money is so called; and drawing the lips tight is the same word as a verb.

clue.text: Like a stonewaller, for example, unlikely to crumple

explanation.surface: A dour defensive batsman, like a good shirt, will not crumple.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a stonewaller is a batsman who blocks every ball, staying in the crease (the marked area at the stumps); fabric so labelled keeps its shape.
explanation.definitionFit: Cloth treated to resist wrinkling; a blocking batsman resists dismissal at his marked line.

clue.text: Batting under strain, concentrated

parts.note: in cricket the side batting is 'in'
someone under strain is tense

explanation.surface: A batsman under pressure is fully focused.
explanation.definitionFit: Strong and focused, as a concentrated flavour or effort is heightened.

clue.text: Two sorts of fish for infant

parts.note: the nurse shark is a fish
the ling is a fish of the cod family

explanation.surface: Two kinds of fish suitable for a baby.
explanation.definitionFit: An old word for a baby being nursed, a suckling.

clue.text: Brilliant finishes an eye-opener in Le Mans, perhaps

indicators.note: in tells us one letter goes within the rearranged race name
perhaps suggests the letters of the place name could be some other arrangement

parts.note: the opener of the word eye is its first letter

explanation.surface: Shiny paintwork on cars at the Le Mans race is a revelation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges the race name to ENAMLS, and 'in' puts the E inside it. Le Mans hosts a famous French 24-hour motor race.
explanation.definitionFit: Glossy hard coatings give a shiny surface to metal or pottery.

clue.text: Inducement used to avoid sugar in tea, perhaps

definitions.text: used to avoid sugar in tea, perhaps

explanation.surface: A bribe helps some swallow a sugar-free cup of tea.
explanation.walkthrough: An inducement is a bribe; an artificial sweetener replaces sugar in tea.
explanation.definitionFit: A bribe that makes a deal attractive; also a sugar substitute such as saccharin.

clue.text: Goes on board with English doctors seizing rescue craft

indicators.note: seizing means the doctors' abbreviation grips the boat word inside it

parts.note: MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's degree; two make MBS
Noah's ark was the vessel that rescued the animals from the flood

explanation.surface: Medics from England grab a lifeboat and climb aboard.
explanation.walkthrough: MB (Bachelor of Medicine) is the British medical degree, so doctors are MBS.
explanation.definitionFit: To set foot on a ship or plane at the start of a journey.

clue.text: Shy in party, almost drunk

parts.note: a bash is an informal party

indicators.note: almost means the word for drunk loses its final letter

parts.note: full is slang for drunk

explanation.surface: A timid person at a party, nearly drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Timid and self-conscious in company.

clue.text: Exhaust unserviceable inside? Stop!

indicators.note: inside means the abbreviation for useless goes within the word for exhaust

parts.note: to spend energy is to exhaust it
US is short for useless, unserviceable

explanation.surface: A car's exhaust is broken inside, so halt!
explanation.walkthrough: 'inside' looks like part of the car-trouble picture; it is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To halt or put off temporarily.

clue.text: Least possible amount-not a penny — for this item

indicators.note: not a penny tells us the penny's letter is to be taken away

parts.note: a particle is the tiniest bit of something

explanation.surface: A shopper wants the cheapest possible price, not even a penny, for this thing.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove P from PARTICLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A single thing in a list or collection, as an article of clothing.

clue.text: Current scholar of Magdalen without a place to study

indicators.note: without means outside, so the joined pieces wrap round the a

parts.note: AC is alternating current
a demy is a foundation scholar at Magdalen College, Oxford

explanation.surface: A present Magdalen scholar lacks anywhere to study.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'lacking' but means outside: AC and DEMY surround A.
explanation.definitionFit: A school or college where people study.

clue.text: A funny person to issue a warning

explanation.surface: A comedian is set to give a warning.
explanation.walkthrough: Old slang calls an amusing person 'a caution'. 'to' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Dated slang for an amusing or outrageous person; also to warn as a verb.

clue.text: Thriller in which things need to be sorted out?

definitions.text: Thriller in which things need to be sorted out?

parts.words: Thriller in which things need to be sorted out?
parts.note: read as a tense story whose plot must be resolved, but really a ledger heading in bookkeeping where uncertain entries are parked until they can be properly allocated

explanation.surface: A mystery novel leaves loose ends for the reader to tie up.
explanation.definitionFit: In bookkeeping, a temporary ledger heading holds unclear items until they are assigned, and the first word also suggests a thriller.

clue.text: Take steps to get missile a degree lower

indicators.note: lower in a down clue puts the degree piece below the missile

parts.note: SAM is a surface-to-air missile
a BA is a degree

explanation.surface: Measures taken to bring a missile down a notch.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer 'lower' puts BA beneath SAM.
explanation.definitionFit: To dance a lively Brazilian dance, moving the feet in rhythm.

clue.text: Given signal by actor about line that's cryptically indicated

indicators.note: about means the cue word goes round the line letter

parts.note: an actor's cue signals another to speak; given one is cued

explanation.surface: An actor's cue prompts a line with a hint.
explanation.walkthrough: L goes inside CUED. 'that's' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Hinted at by a clue, as in a crossword.

clue.text: Man with legal expertise that's not uniform

explanation.surface: A lawyer turns up in plain clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: The two senses are unrelated: an Islamic legal scholar, and civilian dress worn by someone who usually wears uniform.
explanation.definitionFit: A Muslim jurist who gives rulings; also the plain civilian clothes of an off-duty soldier.

clue.text: For example, removing the head of administration

explanation.surface: Firing the boss of a civil service department is one example.
explanation.walkthrough: Beheading is one kind of capital punishment; the same word means carrying out or administering, as with a will.
explanation.definitionFit: Capital punishment, of which beheading is one form; also the carrying out of a plan or will.

clue.text: Editor legally represented, it's said

indicators.note: represented hints that the letters are presented anew in a different order

explanation.surface: An editor, speaking through a lawyer, claims something is reported.
explanation.walkthrough: 'represented' rearranges ED plus LEGALLY.
explanation.definitionFit: Supposedly, according to what people claim without proof.

clue.text: Way in which knight cuts philanthropist

indicators.note: cuts means the chess symbol slices into the middle of the entrance word

parts.note: a door is a way in
N is the chess notation for knight

explanation.surface: A path where a knight slashes at a charitable benefactor.
explanation.walkthrough: N goes inside DOOR.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who gives money or organs freely, a benefactor.
